**ACCEPT** — reviewer of record: PM loop (QA wave #9296), session `session_01Ai9gUdihXjg7FumzsBNSSs`.

Two claims spot-checked against the tree rather than the report, both hold:

- **The objectui unlock is real.** `.cache/objectui-665661ab0932` exists in the QA tree **with `node_modules` present**. That is what let 25 objectui unit pins (249 tests) run at the exact `.objectui-sha` pin with zero installs — the sibling `/home/user/objectui` is at a different sha (`195b9e4ab`) and has none. Without that read, 26 items would have gone `blocked(environment)` on a constraint that was not actually binding. This belongs in RUNNER.md's facts section; folded into #9386.
- **The checklist-accuracy finding is confirmed.** `api-backend.query-contract-matrix` cites `packages/objectql/src/filter-comparand-shape.ts` as an `automated.ref`. That file exists and is a **source module, not a test** — nothing executes it as a pin. The item carries **9 acceptance clauses**, which corroborates the `partial` rather than `pass` scoring.

## The finding that changes the wave's cost model

**39 of 77 pinned items are `partial` because the pin is narrower than the item** — `identity-auth.admin-lifecycle-operations` pins 1 of 10 clauses; `api-backend.query-contract-matrix` (P0) pins one expand path out of nine. Mapping each pin's executed test titles onto its acceptance clauses, and naming every gap, is the most reusable thing this round produced — more so than the 35 PASS.

It also corrects a premise I dispatched on. I framed the 77 pinned items as "cheap coverage, already proven by CI". They are cheap, and 0 failed — but **`automated.ref` present ≠ item covered**. The honest reading is 35 items fully covered, 39 partially, and the remaining clause gaps join the hand-driving load rather than sitting outside it.

## Judgement calls I am endorsing

- **The 11 deterministic objectui live-e2e reds recorded `blocked`/`partial` rather than `fail`.** Four independent lines of evidence, not one: only 4 live specs are on objectui's own CI allowlist (all 4 green here), the lane is `continue-on-error`, the pinned pairing is a *published* backend (`backend.env` → `17.0.0-rc.2`) rather than a source build, and several failures are demonstrable assertion bugs (one fails a strict-mode ambiguity in which the element it sought **was** found). Two are covered by explicit ledger `stale` runnerRules that forbid scoring a FAIL — and the runner reproduced the exact predicted symptom independently. Recording a red as `blocked` needs this much justification, and it was supplied.
- **`objectui e2e/live/ci/backend.env` violating its own stated invariant** (`OBJECTSTACK_VERSION=17.0.0-rc.2` while the lock resolves `@objectstack/spec ^17.0.0-rc.6`, where the file's own header says the two must be bumped together) is a finding **at destination** — it belongs in `objectstack-ai/objectui`, not here. Filing it there is the right next step; it means that lane may currently be testing a pairing it declares meaningless.

## Carried forward

- The three checklist-accuracy defects (source-module-as-pin; two refs naming companion tests by bare name with no path) go into the ledger-edit PR alongside the five from #9334 — one docs-only change with `revision` bumps, not eight scattered edits.
- **`verify --rls`: the `exec` and `auditor` position personas proved NOTHING** — 0 PROVEN, every object member-visible / probe-blocked / skipped. Zero HOLES overall, but as the runner put it, a persona that proves nothing is indistinguishable from a persona with no policy. That deserves its own look before the wave closes; it is not covered by any current item.
- The 11 items pinning objectui live specs objectui itself does not gate should either re-pin to the 4-spec allowlist or record the required backend pairing.

Tier-2A (23 unpinned api/cli/build items) dispatched.

**Close-out — extracted.** Wave #9296, executed under #9480. Nothing re-judged, nothing re-run. **No FAIL to dispose of.** 0 FAIL across 77 items; no product defect and no access-control finding. The four-way disposition therefore has no input from this record, which is exactly what its PARTIAL column says: the pins are green, and the value is in what they do not reach. ## What was extracted The three **security-priority** coverage gaps from this record's own gap list are filed and in the queue — **#9481** (the read side of FLS mask/strip, plus the persona × CRUD cell matrix `verify` cannot see), **#9482** (the admin-lifecycle clauses C0–C7/C9 that the single pinned audit clause leaves open), **#9483** (the unpinned authorization clauses of the attachments chain). They are pin-upgrade cards, not defect cards: the property is untested, not broken. ## (d) invalid pairing / environment — recorded blocked, no card Recorded here so a later reader does not mistake a red for a product signal: - **11 objectui `e2e/live` specs red, deterministically.** Not scored `fail`, and correctly so: only 4 specs (`screen-flow`, `action-modal`, `master-detail`, `saved-view-filter`) are on objectui's own `test:e2e:live:ci` allowlist and **all four passed**; the lane is `continue-on-error: true` and warns against switching the rest on; the pinned pairing is a **published** backend (`OBJECTSTACK_VERSION=17.0.0-rc.2` in `e2e/live/ci/backend.env`) rather than this source build; and at least two of the reds are demonstrably assertion bugs (a strict-mode locator that matched the real `

` twice; a whitelist assertion the product has moved past). A matched-pairing re-run remains worthwhile and is not a clean bill — that stays parked. - **3 items `blocked`**: `inline-grid-receipt-cells`, `related-list-server-pagination`, `record-page-roundtrip` — the last two under the ledger's own `stale` flag whose `runnerRule` says outright not to score the spec's failure as a FAIL. This run reproduced the documented staleness byte-for-byte, which is corroboration of the ledger, not a defect. - **1 skipped cross-tenant attachment probe** — `@objectstack/organizations` is cloud-private and absent from the OSS workspace, so the block skips loudly by design. `blocked(dependency)`. ## Everything else stays parked, by pointer All remaining (non-security) coverage gaps in the "Coverage gaps" section above — query-contract REST clauses, presign envelope shapes, the attachments status pipeline / reap ordering / chunked session, the automation node and trigger matrices, auth-method C0–C6/C9, invitation-scope C4–C6, dashboards, webhook and email lifecycle clauses, nav error surfaces, draft-publish clauses — are parked on the wave anchor by the PM's 2026-08-18 comment. **This record is the authoritative list; do not re-file from memory without reading it.** The five checklist-accuracy findings join the ledger-edit PR.
